quote_zh: Document is English; the source lines and their '> EN:' partners are byte identical, and these are the source lines. Contributing lines, in order: 179, 183, 185, 187, 192, 194, 213, 228. L179 [0031]: "there is provided a process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst." L183 [0032]: "Examples of oxidizing agent include alkali metal hypochlorite and peroxide such as hydrogen peroxide." L185 [0033]: "the ruthenium catalyst is oxidized by the hypochlorite to produce a mixture of ruthenate, perruthenate and ruthenium tetroxide" and "the ruthenium oxide is an insoluble solid present in substantially the same amount as initially so it can be filtered off and reused (for >50 conversion), even without treatment, in another cycle" and "Preferably, in the form of ruthenium dioxide hydrate." L187 and L192 [0034], across the p11 page break: "the ruthenium catalyst can be in the form of salt such as ruthenium trichloride. The catalyst RuO2 can be formed in situ in a reaction commencing" / "with ruthenium trichloride in an aqueous caustic solution containing starting material and purging chlorine gas." L194 [0035], the only conditions statement: "with RuO2 as a catalyst and cheap and readily available sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) as an oxidant.In certain embodiments, the mixture of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV),RuO2 catalyst and sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) can be heated to reflux temperature under stirring for about more than 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, or 5 hours, preferably in the range of about 2 hours to about 8 hours, more preferably for about 6 hours to about 8 hours." Printing faults transcribed as printed: "oxidant.In" and "(IV),RuO2". L213 [0038](i) and L228 [0039](i) repeat the step verbatim of each other: "(i) oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide as a catalyst, to produce 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III)". Lines 192, 213 and 228 are printed in the enriched file with a leading 'None' marker column, which is not document text and is stripped.
arithmetic_check: Nothing to close, and nothing is claimed to close. This section states no mass, no volume, no mole, no equivalent and no molar ratio for any compound, so no mass balance, no molar-mass check and no yield check is possible here; the absence of an inconsistency is not evidence that the numbers close. mass_balance_implausible, molar_mass_inconsistent and scale_discontinuity are therefore not raised and not cleared either. The four numeric statements in this step's prose are all non-quantitative for balance purposes and are recorded as follows. (1) The time preferences in [0035], 'more than 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, or 5 hours', then 'about 2 hours to about 8 hours', then 'about 6 hours to about 8 hours': nested ranges, no single value, so time_h is null and the wording sits in notes. A5 should check that decision, since a scorer may expect 6 or 8 there. (2) '(for >50 conversion)' in [0033]: printed with no unit and no percent sign, left uninterpreted, and not put into process_control.threshold_pct. (3) 'ruthenium (IV)' and 'ruthenium dioxide': oxidation state and stoichiometry in names, not quantities. (4) The formula numbers (III) and (IV) are labels. Reflux and 'commercial scale' give no number. Note for A5: the Example sections of this document do carry masses, moles and yields for this same oxidation, and that is where the arithmetic can actually be tested; this section is the generic recitation of it.

quote_zh: Contributing lines, in order: 198, 209, 211, 215, 230. This method is extremely advantageous over the prior art methods for the preparation of enol ester, in that it does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC)." "In various embodiments, the disclosed process can produce enol ester of formula (II) in high yields, e.g. at least 65%, with a purity of at least 85%. In another embodiment, the disclosed process can produce solvent recovery of >85%." arithmetic_check: Nothing to close, and nothing is claimed to close. This section states no mass, no volume, no mole, no equivalent and no molar ratio for any compound, so no mass balance, no molar-mass check and no yield check is possible here; the absence of an inconsistency is not evidence that the numbers close. mass_balance_implausible, molar_mass_inconsistent and scale_discontinuity are therefore not raised and not cleared either. The three percentage figures in [0037] are FLOORS and are deliberately not in any numeric field: 'in high yields, e.g. at least 65%' is a yield minimum for a class of embodiments, 'with a purity of at least 85%' is a purity minimum, and 'solvent recovery of >85%' is a recovery lower bound on the solvent and not on the product. product_yield_pct and product_purity_pct are null for that reason and not because the figures were missed; the same call was made and confirmed on the same sentence at A1. There is consequently no stated-mass against stated-yield pair to check. A5 should confirm that a floor stays out of a measurement field, and should note that a machine extractor will very likely put 65 and 85 into those two fields, which is a real and expected disagreement rather than a gold-set error. One structural check that CAN be done and does close: the spans give reactants C8H7NO6S and C6H8O2 and product C14H13NO7S, so the condensation balances exactly on the loss of one water, 8+6 carbons, 7+8-2 hydrogens and 6+2-1 oxygens, with nothing else added or lost. Verified with RDKit from the span SMILES. That is consistent with the carbodiimide being the dehydrating agent the prose names.
